_what: Two claims about the Figma file, verified at the destination by an instrument that did not make them: the drawn component library, and the seven skill prompts written into it "verbatim".
_why: `figma-generated.json` is a census taken PLUGIN-SIDE, by the same tool that did the drawing. A generator confirming its own output is the weakest evidence there is - it can only report what it believes it did. This reads the same page through the REST API, a different instrument on a different transport, and pairs the two.

identity._what: Not just the counts. Every census row paired to a live node by ID, and every live set found in the census.

the_finding.claim: THE GENERATED LIBRARY IS A PROJECTION OF THE MEASUREMENT, NOT A COPY OF IT, FOR TWO BLOCKS - AND NOTHING SAID SO.
the_finding.detail: 41 of 43 blocks agree with figma-variants.json on their axis NAMES. Two do not: pagination declares Layout x State and the live set has only Layout; progressbar declares Layout x Size and the live set has only Size.
the_finding.cause: figma-draw.js took `Object.keys(measured.axes)[0]` and dropped the rest with no record. The module comment says the generator "does not decide the axis", which was true of the axis it picked and silent about the one it did not.
the_finding.why_it_matters: This is BREACH-0010's class in different clothes. That breach was that an artefact called GENERATED had no generator; this is a real generator whose output is called a reproduction while it silently narrows its input. Both leave a reader believing a stronger thing than is true, and neither is visible in the artefact - the census reported 43 of 43 sets drawn, 0 refusals, 0 skipped, and it was right about every number it printed.
the_finding.fixed: `specsFor` now carries `droppedAxes`, and the emitted script returns `projectedOntoOneAxis` naming each one. Not a throw: refusing would leave two blocks undrawn, and an undrawn block is worse than a projected one. What was missing was the RECORD.

_what_this_does_not_establish: That the drawn variants LOOK like the measured ones. This pairs identity, counts and axis names; it reads no fill, no radius and no text.
That the 41 agreeing blocks are faithful in any deeper sense - only that their axis names match and their variant counts do.
Anything about the other 18 pages of the file. Only `Library (generated)` was read.

vendored._why: figma-nodes.json quotes page and frame names MEASURED from the Figma file verbatim - "Uber Base - full catalogue", "Index - all 39 block types" - and two of them contain an em dash. The house rule is about prose this repository AUTHORS; rewriting a measured name to suit a style guide would make the manifest disagree with the file it is a census of, and pairing is done BY NAME.
vendored._why_here_and_not_in_that_file:: A file cannot vouch for its own digest: editing it changes the content and the recorded digest together, so the check always passes. The voucher lives in the artefact that VERIFIES the census instead, which couples the two - editing the census breaks the voucher until this verification is re-run, which is the behaviour wanted.

second_finding.claim: EVERY BLOCK TYPE NOW HAS TWO COMPONENT SETS IN THE FILE, and the register cites the older one.
second_finding.measured: The live file holds 89 component sets across 19 pages: 46 hand-built (30 on `Components`, 16 on `Base (redrawn)`) plus the 43 the generator drew on `Library (generated)`. FIGMA_NODES in vds-bridge.js points at the hand-built id for all 43 block types, so `vds impl` sends an implementer to the original while the generator maintains a parallel drawing nobody cites.
second_finding.why_it_matters: BREACH-0010's remedy made the library reproducible, and reproducible turned out to mean "drawn a second time beside the first" rather than "the one that is there". Neither drawing is wrong. What is wrong is that nothing said there were two, and `figma-generated.json` reported `duplicateBlockTypes: 0` truthfully - it counts duplicates WITHIN the generated page and cannot see the file.
second_finding.recorded_as: All 43 are now declared in figma-nodes.json `unpaired`, each naming the hand-built id the register cites instead. The existing pairing gate found them the moment the census stopped being stale, which is the gate working.
second_finding.not_resolved_here: Which drawing should be canonical is a real question and is NOT settled by adding a census row. It bears on SUBMISSION-VDS-011 (what a register row's counterpart is) and is left for the same bench rather than decided by whoever next runs the generator.

staleness_found.claim: THE CENSUS WAS STALE BY ONE PAGE AND 43 SETS, AND NOTHING COULD TELL.
staleness_found.why: `measured_at` was a sentence, not a timestamp, so no instrument could compare it to anything while a reader saw a date and a reason. It is now an ISO instant with the reading command beside it.
staleness_found.how_found: By pointing a SECOND instrument at the same subject. The plugin-side census could not have found this about itself.

prompts_verified._claim: figma-prompts.json says the seven skill prompts were written VERBATIM into the `Prompts (verbatim)` page, and fingerprints each by chars, lines and a trivial checksum the plugin sandbox could recompute.
_checked_two_ways: OFFLINE: each SKILL.md re-read from ~/Documents/agents-final/skill-library and its chars, lines and checksum recomputed. 7 of 7 still match the manifest, so the fingerprints are honest about the source.
AT THE DESTINATION: the seven frames read through the REST API, the body text node of each compared to its source file. 7 of 7 BYTE-IDENTICAL.

frames.114:2: customer-research-engine (added 2026-08-01: the prerequisite headline-lab declares that the pack RUN_ORDER omitted; written verbatim, read back byte-identical, checksum 2733859)

prompts_verified._why_a_clean_result_is_recorded: Three destination checks today produced three findings, and a verification suite that only ever reports findings is one nobody trusts when it reports none. This one passed: the prompts really are verbatim, the manifest really does fingerprint the source it names, and the two agree through a route the writer never used. Recording the pass is what makes the failures credible.
prompts_verified._what_it_does_not_establish: Each frame carries three text nodes and only the LARGEST is compared. The other two are a title and a path label, which are the frame's own furniture and are not claimed to be verbatim anything. Nor does this say the prompts are GOOD, only that the drawing matches the file.
